result: All four criteria pass at 135c8c1. The built-in review raised six findings. I confirmed the behavior ones but rate all as optional, because no current source triggers them. Everything below was run in the worktree.

changed: none (read-only)

checks:
- `/code-review 0e71e52...135c8c1` ran through the Skill tool and returned six findings.
- `bunx --no-install mise run verify` exited 0 with 1766 pass, 0 fail. Log: `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-holyagent/43946df6-456d-58c6-bea3-7e958fcb9495/scratchpad/verify.log`.
- `bunx --no-install mise run build` exited 0 and `git status --short` was empty afterwards. The commit touches no `dist/` file, so the Claude output is byte-identical.
- The previous `stripCitations`, copied into the scratchpad, fails the new tests. The code-span, tilde-fence and unclosed-fence tests fail outright. Three of the seven blank-line cases fail in LF (the two-adjacent-comments cases and the leading-comment case). All seven fail in CRLF.
- Old and new `stripCitations` give identical output on all 272 `.md` files under `packages/runtime/src/instructions`. No current source is affected.

blockers: none

questions: none

notes (optional; probes were run against the new code):
1. The inline-span alternative pairs backticks across list items. `"- it's a ` tick <!-- K1 -->\n- another ` tick\n"` is returned unchanged, so the note would ship to the model. Source: `skills.ts:48`.
2. A fenced block indented 4 or more spaces (list-nested) that contains a blank line loses its comment. `"- a\n\n    ```md\n    one\n\n    <!-- keep -->\n    ```\n"` returns without the comment. Source: `skills.ts:44`.
3. A comment on the last line of the text with no final newline now drops the previous newline. `"x\n<!-- a -->"` returns `"x"`, where the old code returned `"x\n"`. The `agents.ts` caller trims. The skills caller at `skills.ts:218` does not trim, but no current source ends this way.
4. The `docs/development.md` Instruction text paragraph (around line 83) says every generator strips such comments and keeps only the two markers. It does not mention that code spans and fenced blocks are now left as written.
5. The tests have no CRLF coverage for fences and spans, and none for a comment at the end of the text or an indented fence. The four-alternative regex with numbered backreferences is hard to maintain. A line-based fence scanner would be simpler.
6. The `writing-bar.md` and `state-changes.md` edits are scoped as described and need nothing more.

Not run: the Kimi generator output. Only the Claude `dist/` was checked, and the 272-file comparison covers the strip function on the sources.
